title: Property (S_k) ascends along flat maps with (S_k) fibres
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $k\ge0$ an integer. Assume (1) $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], (2) $S$ is Noetherian, (3) $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], (4) for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (a Noetherian ring) has property $(S_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], and (5) $R$ has property $(S_k)$. Then $S$ has property $(S_k)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0339 (lemma-Sk-goes-up, line 46403) and its proof (via Lemma Tag 0337 lemma-apply-grothendieck, depth formula for flat local maps, and Lemma Tag 00OM lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total)

proof.text: Fix a target prime q, and put p = q.comap(algebraMap R S). Use the fibre Noetherian witness supplied by hfibres. PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber supplies the prime Q of p.Fiber S whose inverse image is q.

Apply the proved local fibre depth and height formulas. They give depth(S_q) = depth(R_p) + depth(C_Q) and q.height = p.height + Q.height. Equality of the bundled prime spectra transports the dependent depth expression without changing its local-ring instance.

The base and fibre Serre hypotheses bound these depth terms below by min(k,p.height) and min(k,Q.height). For extended naturals a,b, min(k,a+b) <= min(k,a)+min(k,b): if k<=a or k<=b, the corresponding summand is k and the other is nonnegative; otherwise both minima are a and b. Adding the two bounds and substituting the formulas proves the Serre condition at q.
